we propose a framework that can handle documents of arbitrary length by extending the input of the language models and using the attention to identify the important parts of the input.
we propose a novel method to extend the input of LMs to handle documents of any length.
we propose a new framework for adapting pretrained language models for long document classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of document classification,

the following: (i) How can we adapt pretrained LMs to handle long documents? (ii) How does the performance of the pretrained LMs vary as the length of the input increases? (iii) What is the best way to utilize the pretrained LM in a downstream task?

the following questions: How can pretrained LMs be adapted to handle long documents? Can we use pretrained LMs to achieve human-level performance on long document classification? How can we improve performance on long document text classification?

our method outperforms state of the art methods in both patent and Arxiv dataset.

our proposed method is able to outperform the state-of-the-art methods in both datasets.

our method can be applied to a large class of NLP tasks and is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of a single recurrent layer is sufficient to achieve state-of-the-art performance, while using attention to identify the relevant segments of the input.
the addition of recurrent layers to LMs can be used to handle documents of any length, while still retaining the power of pretrained LMs.
the addition of a simple recurrent mechanism and attention mechanism can greatly improve the classification performance of LMs on long text.
